title: A school bus tracker parents can trust
summary: Show parents where the bus is, and tell them when it is near, on phones and roads that drop out.
context: Lalbagh Learning runs 700 school buses in Bengaluru. An attendant carries a phone that reports location and marks each child on and off. Parents open the app every morning between 7:00 and 8:30, nearly all at once.
Traffic on Outer Ring Road makes timetables useless, and parents want a nudge when the bus is ten minutes away. A child's location is sensitive: only that child's family may follow that bus.
must_handle: A location shown to a parent is at most about 30 seconds old, or it says it is older.
The attendant's phone keeps recording through a dead zone and catches up afterwards.
A parent gets one nudge per trip, at about ten minutes away.
Only a family with a child on that bus today can see it.
History is kept only as long as the school needs it.
show_in_answer: How a location reaches a parent's screen.
How the arrival estimate is made, and how it behaves when the phone goes quiet.
How access is checked for each parent.
What is kept, for how long, and why.
